name: SpreSuite
tagline: An enterprise analytics dashboard for tracking billing, recovery, and payment performance over time.
description:
SpreSuite is business software built around financial operations. The interface presents billing, recovery, and payment data as a multi-series dashboard so operators can compare sales, collections, and recovery across months instead of reconciling those figures in spreadsheets.

The product is an Angular frontend with a Node.js backend, MariaDB for persistent records, Chart.js for visualization, and Kafka plus ELK in the supporting stack. There is no public repository for this work, so the write-up stays limited to the dashboard that can be shown and the technologies used to build it.

coverImage.alt: SpreSuite dashboard showing a Billing-Recovery-Payment grouped bar chart comparing Sales, Payment, and Recovery by month

screenshots.alt: SpreSuite Billing-Recovery-Payment chart with Sales, Payment, and Recovery series from late 2019 through 2024

problem: Finance and operations teams often track sales, payments, and recovery in separate reports. That makes it hard to see whether billed revenue is actually being collected, and where recovery is lagging, in a single view.
approach: Built a dashboard-first Angular application on a Node.js API, with MariaDB as the system of record. Chart.js renders the financial series. Kafka and ELK sit in the surrounding stack for event movement and operational logging rather than as the primary user-facing layer.
solution: A web dashboard that plots billing, recovery, and payment side by side over time. The visible surface is a grouped bar chart titled Billing-Recovery-Payment, with Sales, Payment, and Recovery as separate series so month-to-month collection performance is readable at a glance.
features: Billing-recovery-payment dashboard comparing Sales, Payment, and Recovery over time
Chart.js visualizations for financial performance series
Angular frontend for the operator-facing analytics UI
MariaDB as the relational store for billing and payment records
architecture: Angular client → Node.js API → MariaDB. Chart.js renders dashboard series in the browser. Kafka is used in the event/messaging layer, and ELK is used for logging and operational visibility around that stack.
